notes.claim: Piping and instrument drawings show valves in their normal position unless stated otherwise, usually the primary flowpath of the system.
A checklist for safe isolation asks whether the isolation points on the plant match the line diagram and isolation certificate.
Gate and globe valves are often drawn with the same symbol; the valve's tag number or the drawing's notes and legend may say which it is.
A diaphragm actuator's symbol alone does not say whether air pressure opens or closes the valve.
A three-way valve is sometimes drawn in the position it fails to, not its normal position.
When a print shows two piping systems of the same kind, extra letters on the symbols tell them apart.

sources.title: Engineering Symbology, Prints, and Drawings, Module 2: Engineering Fluid Diagrams and Prints (DOE-HDBK-1016/1-93)
sources.quote: Unless otherwise stated, P&IDs indicate valves in their "normal" position. This is usually interpreted as the normal or primary flowpath for the system. An exception is safety systems, which are normally shown in their standby or non-accident condition.

sources.title: The safe isolation of plant and equipment (HSG253)
sources.quote: Are all isolation points identified on the plant and do they match the line diagram and isolation certificate?

sources.title: Engineering Symbology, Prints, and Drawings, Module 2: Engineering Fluid Diagrams and Prints (DOE-HDBK-1016/1-93)
sources.quote: globe and gate valves will often be depicted by the same valve symbol. In such cases, information concerning the valve type may be conveyed by the component identification number or by the notes and legend section of the drawing

sources.title: Engineering Symbology, Prints, and Drawings, Module 2: Engineering Fluid Diagrams and Prints (DOE-HDBK-1016/1-93)
sources.quote: the symbols alone in Figure 3 do not provide the reader with enough information to determine whether applying air pressure to the diaphragm opens or closes the process control valve

sources.title: Engineering Symbology, Prints, and Drawings, Module 2: Engineering Fluid Diagrams and Prints (DOE-HDBK-1016/1-93)
sources.quote: 3-way valves are sometimes drawn in the position that they will fail to instead of always being drawn in their "normal" position.

sources.title: Basic Diagrams and Systems | Engineering Library (US Navy NAVEDTRA 14105A, Fluid Power, chapter 12)
sources.quote: When a print shows more than one piping system of the same kind, additional letters are added to the symbols to differentiate between the systems.
